standard_full: ISO 8734:1997 (parallel pins of hardened steel and martensitic stainless steel, dowel pins; = DIN EN ISO 8734:1998). c and the upper end of the commercial length range as printed by the pages used.

sources.what: ISO 8734-1997 table: d Nominal Size (m6), d max, d min, c ≈ (d 1-20); no length table in the HTML -> c only
DIN EN ISO 8734 (1998): table d / c and matrix headed 'DIN EN ISO 8734 - commercial lengths' (X marks, nominal length 3-100 by size)
ISO 8734 table: d m6, c, l nominal/min/max with '+' marks under the heading 'trade lengths' (the DIN/6325 page of the site is the identical table)
'ISO Metric Dowel Pins per DIN EN ISO 8734': d = m6, c ≈, L nominal/min/max with x marks, legend 'X = Range of Nominal Lengths'. Its marks start at 16 for d 8 and at 50 for d 16 (others: 18 and 40)
manufacturer product page ISO 8734: d m6, c ≈, c tol., and a list of lengths per diameter under the bare heading 'l' (the maker's own programme) -> counted for c, not for the standard's length range
ISO 8734 B data page: d (incl. 25), m6 limits, C, unlabelled length list per diameter (wider product range) -> counted for c only
dealer page 'ISO 8734 -A-': d 1.5-8, d max/min, c ~; the matrix below is stock quantities, not used
NOT counted: table headed 'DIN Technische Daten' on a DIN 6325 page (l2, r, z1, z2 of the old standard) with an extra row c; the page does not say that row is ISO 8734, and it prints 0,98 for d 5

NOT counted: reproduces the standard's table with its footnotes, the words 'Range of commercial lengths' and the requirements table (material, hardness, surface, workmanship, acceptability) almost verbatim; the range marks are not in the HTML text

dropped.what: lMinStd column (lower end of the commercial length range)
dropped.why: d 8: 18 on fasten.it and fasteners.eu, 16 on engineersedge; d 16: 40 on fasten.it and fasteners.eu, 50 on engineersedge -> only 2 clusters that call their marks the standard's commercial / trade / nominal length range. The researcher's third cluster was the OPAC product page, whose length list stands under a bare 'l' heading in a maker's catalogue table (what the company supplies), and fastenerdata's list is a wider unlabelled range (d 8 from 16, d 16 from 30). The other eleven diameters had 3 clusters (3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 22, 26, 50), but the column was dropped rather than the two common diameters.

dropped.what: d m6 limits (d max / d min)
dropped.why: not a candidate column; not evaluated

dropped.what: old DIN 6325 dimensions (l2, r, z1, z2) and d 14
dropped.why: different standard, not part of the candidate table

checks: c: identical in 6-7 clusters for every diameter (globalfastener, fasten.it, fasteners.eu, engineersedge, OPAC, fastenerdata; + dm-muehl for d 1.5-8)

lMaxStd: identical in exactly 3 clusters for every diameter (fasten.it 'commercial lengths', fasteners.eu 'trade lengths', engineersedge 'range of nominal lengths'); OPAC's catalogue list ends at the same lengths (not counted)
c increases strictly with d and c / d lies between 0.15 and 0.21: True
lMaxStd never decreases with d: True
each length matrix is contiguous (no gaps between the first and last mark of a diameter)
shape_hint: Plain cylindrical pin, ground, diameter tolerance m6; one end has a lead-in chamfer of length c, the other end is rounded/chamfered. No head, no thread.

role_map.c: length of the end chamfer, approximate (pages: c ≈, c ~, 'c =', C)
role_map.lMaxStd: longest nominal length inside the range the pages mark as commercial / trade lengths for that diameter (the table of the standard continues above 100 mm in 20 mm steps)

notes: Verified record: 13 rows x 3 columns (d, c, lMaxStd). lMaxStd is computed by program as the largest marked nominal length per diameter in each matrix. The lower end of the range is not published: pages disagree for d 8 (18 / 18 / 16) and d 16 (40 / 40 / 50). The catalogue code that used lMinStd as a default pin length will find no value.
scope: ISO 8734의 끝 모따기 c와 상업 길이 범위의 위쪽 끝만 — 상업 길이의 아래쪽 끝은 공개 자료끼리 d 8·d 16에서 달라 싣지 않았습니다

verification.checks_done: All pages re-downloaded by the verifier with curl (browser User-Agent) on 2026-11-11 into a separate directory (HTTP 200, text/html); tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (html.parser grid with rowspan/colspan), not the researcher's scripts or raw files. Pages: globalfastener detail_260, fasten.it din_en_iso_8734, fasteners.eu ISO/8734 + DIN/6325, engineersedge 13805, opac producto-166, fastenerdata iso8734b, dm-muehl 8734, theo-schrauben DIN-6325 + ISO-8734, boltport iso-8734. 13 diameters x (c, first and last marked length) re-extracted from every matrix; captions of each length list read to see what the list claims to be.
problems: lMinStd removed (2 clusters at d 8 and d 16). What each page calls its length list: fasten.it 'DIN EN ISO 8734 - commercial lengths' and fasteners.eu 'trade lengths' (standard's range: d 8 from 18, d 16 from 40); engineersedge 'X = Range of Nominal Lengths' per DIN EN ISO 8734 (d 8 from 16, d 16 from 50); OPAC a list under 'l' in a product table with an order reference (company programme, equal to fasten.it/fasteners.eu for all 13 diameters); fastenerdata an unlabelled list incl. d 25 (wider range); dm-muehl stock quantities. Counting OPAC as the standard's range, as the researcher did, is what gave 3.

lMaxStd kept with zero slack (fasten.it, fasteners.eu, engineersedge for all 13 diameters). The same engineersedge matrix is the one that differs at the lower end for d 8 and d 16, so its upper ends agree but the page is not flawless. The lead may prefer to drop lMaxStd too and keep d and c only (c has 6-7 clusters).
theo-schrauben's c row (DIN 6325 page, 0,98 for d 5) and dm-muehl's stock matrix are not counted; Boltport's ISO 8734 page is a near-verbatim reproduction and stays excluded.

Not counted, for the lead's information: the publisher-authorised preview service (standards.iteh.ai sample PDF, a T1-type source under app/SOURCE_RULE.md) shows the dimension table of this ISO standard; the kept values equal it. The table could be re-based on that official preview instead of T2. (ISO 8734:1997 preview: d and c ≈ rows complete and equal; the length-range part of the table is cut off after l = 16, where the stepped line puts the start for d 8 at 18.)
